title: Attempting square-root prime error and uniform Laguerre cancellation
question: can either remaining route prove the subexponential arithmetic seam bound?

verdict.conclusion: both attempts reach the same boundary. The generalized Li disk is exactly the half-plane Re(s)>1/2. A prime-error exponent theta>1/2 leaves coefficient base (1+theta)/(2-theta)>1, while direct subexponential Laguerre cancellation would analytically continue the endpoint-completed prime logarithm through that same half-plane. No established TTI identity or unconditional prime estimate crosses it.

routeA_squareRootPrimeError.target: psi(x)-x=O(x^(1/2) log^2 x), or more generally O_epsilon(x^(1/2+epsilon)) for every epsilon>0
routeA_squareRootPrimeError.explicitFormula: psi(x)-x is governed by sums of x^rho/rho; a zero with Re(rho)=beta>1/2 contributes at x^beta scale and obstructs a uniform square-root bound

attemptedInputs.outcome: controls only an exponent tending down from one, not one half
improves the x-scale by a subpower factor but does not produce x^(1/2+epsilon)
moves any first counterexample upward but gives no all-height prime-error exponent

attemptedInputs.input: positive central horizontal residue and seam contraction
attemptedInputs.outcome: supplies an RH-equivalent zero-side norm but no inequality for psi(x)-x

routeA_squareRootPrimeError.blockingEquivalence: the square-root Chebyshev estimate excludes every beta>1/2; functional symmetry then gives RH. Deriving it without new arithmetic input would already be a proof of RH

attemptedInputs.outcome: the prime-error multiplier lies at the critical weighted boundary; available unconditional error does not supply the needed critical L2 or pointwise norm

attemptedInputs.input: Cauchy-Schwarz after taking a weighted L2 norm
attemptedInputs.outcome: requires a critical weighted norm not supplied by unconditional estimates; the later all-scale Chebyshev-energy theorem is weaker in pointwise form but still RH-equivalent
introduces new logarithmic prime moments and does not close to a contractive recurrence for p_n

attemptedInputs.input: signed oscillation of the Chebyshev error
attemptedInputs.outcome: neither its phase nor its correlation with all Laguerre kernels is controlled uniformly in n

routeB_uniformLaguerreCancellation.blockingEquivalence: a subexponential coefficient bound gives radius at least one and hence zero-freeness of (s-1)zeta(s) through Re(s)>1/2; this is RH after functional symmetry

quantitativeBoundary.interpretation: theta=1/2 gives B=1. Every fixed theta>1/2 gives B>1, so even an arbitrarily small fixed loss above square-root scale remains exponential in n

whyAveragingDoesNotClosePointwiseControl.statement: available zero-density and averaged-in-height estimates can bound most ordinates, but the seam infimum and coefficient radius are changed by one exceptional zero; the later critical all-X energy target is stronger
whyAveragingDoesNotClosePointwiseControl.consequence: an exceptional-set theorem cannot replace a uniform all-zero or all-n estimate

strongestConditionalClosure.laguerrePremise: equivalently, p_n=O_epsilon(exp(epsilon n)) for every epsilon>0
strongestConditionalClosure.conclusion: either premise gives radius one, seam infimum one, and RH
strongestConditionalClosure.status: both premises remain unproved and equivalent in strength to the target

newExactInformation: the two proposed routes are the same analytic-continuation problem in different coordinates
the loss from a prime-error exponent theta is exactly the coefficient base (1+theta)/(2-theta)
Laguerre orthogonality reaches a critical weighted boundary rather than supplying a free positivity theorem
proofBoundary.missingTheorem: a genuinely new arithmetic inequality excluding every zero in Re(s)>1/2, expressed either as square-root Chebyshev error or uniform signed-Laguerre cancellation
proofBoundary.status: neither attempted route proves the missing theorem; RH remains open
